{"answers":[{"question_id":"Q016_pdb_1acc_domain_split","answer":"SCOP 1.75 represented PDB 1acc chain A, anthrax protective antigen, as one whole-chain domain: d1acca_ (SUNID 43828), family f.11.1.1. Its fold and superfamily were both named Anthrax protective antigen, within class f, Membrane and cell surface proteins and peptides.

In SCOPe 2.06 and 2.08, that assignment is split into two domains, with ranges in PDB residue numbering:
• d1acca2 (SUNID 238522), A:14–225: PA14 family b.179.1.1, PA14-like superfamily b.179.1, Anthrax protective antigen N-terminal-like fold b.179, class b (All beta proteins).
• d1acca1 (SUNID 238521), A:226–735: Anthrax protective antigen C-terminal-like family f.60.1.1, superfamily f.60.1, and fold f.60, retaining class f.

This is an evolutionary reinterpretation of the same protein, not a biological change between releases. It recognizes the N-terminal PA14 region as a separately classifiable evolutionary module rather than treating the entire chain as one indivisible unit. A protein can combine modules with different evolutionary histories; classification boundaries are revisable hypotheses informed by comparative evidence. Family membership supports a closer evolutionary relationship, superfamily membership supports broader common ancestry, while fold or class similarity alone does not establish homology. The split itself does not establish a particular historical fusion event.

Homology searches should therefore query or model these regions separately and inspect which domain each alignment actually covers. A PA14-region match can support regional homology without establishing homology across the C-terminal region or the complete protein. Whole-chain searches remain useful for comparing domain architectures, but should not obscure local relationships. Do not transfer protective-antigen function, whole-chain template suitability, or exact target boundaries from a match to just one module; those require additional sequence, structural, and functional evidence. Record the SCOPe release and update legacy d1acca_ references to the appropriate split domain when building search or representative sets.","evidence_used":["Pretrained knowledge of domain evolution and homology-search interpretation","mcp__scope__get_scop_service_info","mcp__scope__get_scop_pdb_entry","mcp__scope__get_scop_domains","/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/current","/api/v1/releases/1.75/pdb/1acc","/api/v1/releases/1.75/pdb/1acc/domains","/api/v1/releases/1.75/sids/d1acca_","/api/v1/releases/1.75/sids/d1acca_/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.06/pdb/1acc/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/pdb/1acc/domains","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1acca1","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1acca1/parents","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1acca2","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sids/d1acca2/parents"]}]}
